subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 1: New Media – Grammar and Vocabulary
outcomes: Compare things with more … than, the most, as … as and not as … as.
Decide if a statement about a chart is True, False or Not Given.
Understand and use phrasal verbs like log in and come across.

tf.s: After 'not as … as' we use the base form of the adjective.
tf.why: Yes! We say 'not as big as', not 'not as bigger as'.

tf.s: 'Ahmed is not as tall as Salim' means Ahmed is taller.
tf.why: It means Salim is taller than Ahmed.

tf.s: 'Not Given' means the chart or text gives no information to decide.
tf.why: Correct, you cannot say true or false.

tf.s: 'I am not as taller as my brother' is a correct sentence.
tf.why: The correct form is 'not as tall as'.

tf.s: The meaning of a phrasal verb is not always the meaning of its separate words.
tf.why: Right, phrasal verbs are often idiomatic.

tf.s: In the cartoon, 'bring up' can mean 'raise a child'.
tf.why: Yes, it can also mean 'take upstairs', which causes the joke.

tf.s: 'Log in' is a verb + preposition phrasal verb.
tf.why: 'Log in' is verb + adverb; 'go into' is verb + preposition.

tf.s: 'Taxis are more expensive than buses' = 'Buses are not as expensive as taxis.'
tf.why: Well done, both sentences have the same meaning.

tf.s: To change 'more … than' to 'not as … as', we keep the two items in the same order.
tf.why: We swap the two items: the second one comes first.

boxes.q: Muscat is bigger than Nizwa. = Nizwa is not as ___ as Muscat.
Salim is taller than Ahmed. = Ahmed is ___ as tall as Salim.
boxes.why: 'Not as tall as' shows Ahmed is shorter.

boxes.q: Eating fast food is not as ___ as eating salad.
I ___ a very interesting website last night.

boxes.why: We say 'hurry up' when someone is late.

boxes.q: Which sentence uses a phrasal verb?
The chart has no ages. 'It shows ages' is ...
boxes.why: There is no information about ages, so it is NG.
It has three parts: keep + up + with.

boxes.q: Which word completes: 'TV is the ___ popular activity'?
boxes.why: 'The most' compares one thing with all the others.

hunt.q: Move down a page of posts

o: a verb with an adverb or preposition that makes a new meaning
a verb in the past tense
mcq.why: Phrasal verbs like 'log in' have their own meaning.

mcq.q: In the cartoon, what does 'brought you up' mean in the man's answer?
mcq.why: The joke uses the two meanings of 'bring up'.

mcq.q: Which structure shows two things are equal?
What does 'NG' mean in a True/False/Not Given task?
o: There is no information to decide.
mcq.why: Not Given means the information is not there.

mcq.q: Rewrite: 'My ticket to New York is more expensive than my ticket to Mumbai.'
o: My ticket to Mumbai is not as expensive as my ticket to New York.
My ticket to New York is not as expensive as my ticket to Mumbai.
My ticket to Mumbai is not as more expensive as my ticket to New York.
My ticket to Mumbai is as expensive as my ticket to New York.
mcq.why: Swap the items and use the base adjective.

o: Donkeys are not as heavy as camels.
Camels are not as heavy as donkeys.
Donkeys are not as heavier as camels.
Donkeys are as heavy as camels.
mcq.why: The lighter animal comes first with 'not as … as'.

o: Watching swimming is not as exciting as watching football.
Watching swimming is not as more exciting as watching football.
Watching swimming is not exciting as as watching football.
Watching swimming not as exciting than watching football.
mcq.why: The pattern is not as + adjective + as.

mcq.q: Why is 'not as bigger as' wrong?
o: The adjective after as … as stays in its base form.

mcq.q: Why are phrasal verbs hard to understand by translating each word?
o: They are only used in writing.
mcq.why: The whole phrase has a new meaning.

mcq.q: Why is the cartoon about 'bring up' funny?
o: The two men understand 'bring up' in different ways.
mcq.why: One means 'take upstairs', the other 'raise a child'.
